WRONG AS FILED -- the proposed change would weaken security. Closing as will-not-do with the reasoning, not as stale.

LeafIdent is the identifier NoCheckShim uses to recognise "this is the OCSP responder cert, SKIP revocation checking on it" (RFC 6960 4.2.2.2.1 id-pkix-ocsp-nocheck). It compares (issuer DN, serial) by byte-level DER equality.

The bead says to use names_match instead. That is the right comparator for a REJECTION decision -- which is exactly where lnnl.6 just used it -- and the wrong one for a BYPASS decision. names_match does RFC 4518-style normalisation (case folding, whitespace, BMPString transcoding, bijective AVA matching), so it is strictly more permissive than byte equality. Loosening the test that decides whether to skip revocation means skipping revocation on a certificate that merely normalises equal to the responder. That is a security weakening, and the direction of the error is the dangerous one.

It would also break in the opposite direction. names_match is fail-closed above MAX_AVAS_PER_RDN: an RDN with more AVAs than the cap never matches anything. A legitimate responder whose issuer DN carries such an RDN would stop matching its own identifier, the bypass would not fire, and the recursive OCSP loop the bypass exists to prevent would be required instead.

The existing choice is also already justified in place (lib.rs:1548-1551): both sides originate from the same parsed chain, so the DER is identical and byte equality is exact. Verified that premise rather than taking the comment on trust -- leaf_id is LeafIdent::of(&chain[0]) at lib.rs:1410, and both matches() call sites (check_revocation, check_revocation_against_anchor) receive certificates from that same chain. The comment even states the correct caveat: this would NOT be right for cross-origin comparison.

No code change. If anything the rustdoc could say "a bypass decision must not use a normalising comparator" explicitly, since the current note explains why byte equality is sufficient but not why names_match would be unsafe; filed nothing for that as the existing note plus this record covers it.
